patch.value:
## Problem

The .gitattributes merge fence is generated per item-type directory, so it
covers every tracked item document and both append-only streams. It does not
cover tracked **JSON state that is not an item**, and two such files exist.

Verified 2026-07-26 with git check-attr on every tracked file under .agents/pm:

```
.agents/pm/settings.json                        merge: pm-json      OK
.agents/pm/schema/*.json                        merge: pm-json      OK
.agents/pm/extensions/.managed-extensions.json  merge: unspecified  GAP
.agents/pm/search/eval-queries.json             merge: unspecified  GAP
```

Tracked-file census under .agents/pm: 2,109 .jsonl, 2,098 .toon, 7 .json.
The .toon and .jsonl populations are fully fenced. Two of the seven JSON files
are not.

## Why .managed-extensions.json is the sharp one

It is the *only* tracked file under .agents/pm/extensions, it is the
authoritative record of which extensions a workspace has installed, and it
changes often — `pnpm changelog:pm` regeneration touches it as a side effect,
which is why the release runbook already tells maintainers to check it out
before committing.

Its payload is an `entries[]` array of per-extension objects. Under git's
default line-level merge, two agents on two branches that each install a
different extension produce overlapping insertions into the same array region.
That is a textual conflict on a file that pm itself wrote and that no human is
expected to hand-resolve — and it lands in exactly the multi-agent,
multi-branch workflow the merge fence exists to protect. The pm-json driver
already performs key-level JSON merging and is already wired for settings.json
and schema/*.json; the fence simply never lists this path.

## Scope

- No new merge driver is required; pm-json already exists and is registered by
  `pm merge install`.
- The fence generator has to enumerate tracked non-item JSON state, not just
  item-type directories, or the same gap reappears the next time a subsystem
  adds a tracked JSON file.
- Untracked/derived directories (checkpoints, locks, runtime, search index
  payloads) correctly need no driver — they carry 0 tracked files. Only
  eval-queries.json inside .agents/pm/search is tracked.

## Verification recipe

```
for f in $(git ls-files .agents/pm | grep -E '\.json$'); do
  printf '%s ' "$f"; git check-attr merge -- "$f" | sed 's/.*merge: //'
done
```
Any `unspecified` row is a gap.
The merge fence covers item documents but not tracked non-item JSON, so .managed-extensions.json line-conflicts between agents on different branches

git check-attr over every tracked file under .agents/pm shows .agents/pm/extensions/.managed-extensions.json and .agents/pm/search/eval-queries.json resolve to merge: unspecified, so git falls back to line-level merge on pm-authored JSON state while settings.json and schema/*.json correctly get the pm-json driver.

git check-attr merge reports a pm driver for every tracked file under .agents/pm, with zero unspecified rows; The .gitattributes fence generator derives its JSON entries from tracked non-item state so a newly tracked JSON file is fenced automatically; A regression test merges two branches that each install a different extension and asserts .managed-extensions.json reconciles without conflict markers
Closes the last textual-conflict surface in tracked pm state so parallel agents merge cleanly without manual repair.
Two agents installing different extensions on different branches hit a conflict in an entries[] array that pm wrote and pm should reconcile.
Every tracked non-item JSON file under .agents/pm resolves to a pm merge driver, and the fence generator enumerates tracked JSON state rather than item-type directories alone.

Multi-agent branch work is the workflow the merge fence exists to protect, and the extension manifest is both the most frequently rewritten tracked JSON and the one no human is expected to hand-resolve.

patch.value: Package-owned release history for the full context-integrity bundle
Implemented generalized tracked-JSON merge fencing, conservative additive-array reconciliation, portable installed-driver recognition, SDK documentation, and regression coverage.
Concurrent branches can merge every tracked non-item JSON document and additive JSON arrays without losing independent additions, while semantic edits still conflict.
The generated JSON fence now covers nested tracker JSON, three-way JSON merging unions only additive arrays, and a real two-branch managed-extension merge succeeds through the installed driver.
